title: Big Watt, PowerHouse secure approval for hyperscale data center campus in Texas
key_facts: Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers announced approval of the development agreement for the Taylor Technology Campus near Taylor, Texas, according to a press release.
The campus sits on 664 acres and could support up to one gigawatt of hyperscale data center capacity.

The agreement sets project-specific standards for water use, stormwater, site design, landscaping, setbacks, lighting and noise, and includes developer-funded upgrades to Taylor's reclaimed-water system.
The campus plans dedicated behind-the-meter power from natural gas; power availability is targeted for the first half of 2028.
The Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) is tracking 438,000 MW of large-load requests, nearly 89 percent from data centers.

Construction Review reports the Taylor City Council voted unanimously on 8 Oct 2026 to approve the annexation agreement, over objections from many residents, after the developers had withdrawn an earlier application.
Construction is targeted for 2027 through 2029, according to Construction Review.
quote_evidence: The campus will have the potential to support up to one gigawatt of hyperscale data center capacity.
Power availability at the campus is targeted for the first half of 2028, aligning power delivery with data center deployment schedules.
The Taylor City Council voted unanimously on October 8 to approve an agreement annexing the 664-acre Taylor Technology Campus, a data center and on-site power project near Austin, Texas.
why_it_matters_hint: A 1 GW Texas campus with its own gas power plant has cleared a local approval step, over resident objections.
event_date: City council vote Thu 8 Oct 2026; companies' announcement 13 Oct 2026
notes: Follow-up of a story in our 10 Oct pool ('Taylor OKs data center and power plant campus amid resident opposition'). New today: the companies' own announcement with the standards and the 2028 power target. W.Media relies on a press release.
